title: Baker Mayfield is ‘more relatable’ than Tom Brady. Some of his Buccaneers teammates explain why
content:
In his early NFL days with the Cleveland Browns, Baker Mayfield starred in a series of commercials in which he was stumped by his circuit breaker, had his plumbing malfunction, and fought with his push lawn mower.

Mayfield’s relatability is an often-overlooked quality in the undersized, uber-confident quarterback, who has aggressively navigated a career of chaos — at least until he found a home with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Now, about to start his fourth season with the Bucs, Mayfield has found his comfort zone. As The Athletic’s Zak Keefer revealed in a feature published Thursday, those in the organization — top to bottom — relate to Mayfield even more than a certain legend who led them to a Super Bowl championship.

“I would never throw shade on Tom because I like my ring too much,” general manager Jason Licht said, referencing his Super Bowl LV finery Tom Brady earned him in 2021, “but Baker is just more … relatable.”

As Keefer’s story reveals, Mayfield is quick to engage with his teammates in life’s simple pleasures, like video games and beer-chugging at sporting events. But he is also charitable with his energy and time. To his fellow Buccaneers, that care is obvious. Mayfield foots the bill for their recovery visits with his personal physiotherapist, for example, and he spends time with his teammates off the field.

“Tom really didn’t do anything with us, because he couldn’t. Like, he couldn’t even go to dinner,” said tackle Tristan Wirfs, Mayfield’s closest friend on the team. “Then Baker comes in, and the first day he’s here he asks me if I wanna grab a beer that night. I’m like, ‘This is sick!'”

Mayfield’s comfort level with his teammates has created a chemistry that has led to impressive feats, like his 41-touchdown campaign in 2024. It has also earned him a legion of teammates willing to flock to his side for a fight — more than likely started by Mayfield — and a head coach and general manager who let him be his fiery, fearless self.

“He fits us,” Licht said, “because he came to a place where (head coach Todd Bowles) and the GM said, ‘Hey, be you.’”

Or as Zach Austin, Mayfield’s best friend at Texas Tech, put it: “He’s the best teammate I’ve ever had.”
